messages:
Alex Z: Heads-up — RFC follow-up: we need to nail the shim routing policy for v1->v2 migration. Major goal: zero-downtime for hosted while allowing customers to opt in to new behavior.
Maya R: +1. Can we pick one approach and stop bikeshedding? Two options I see: cluster-level compat gateway vs per-service shim.
Samir P: I prefer gateway for hosted — centralizes metrics and rollback. But it adds latency and single point to scale.
Leah T: Per-service shim keeps latency low and allows teams to iterate independently. Downside: duplicates logic and more surface area for bugs.
Dave: Important constraint: streaming and SSE. Gateway breaks streaming semantics unless we proxy passthrough at TCP level which is messy.
Alex Z: Good call on streaming. If we go gateway we need a passthrough mode for streaming endpoints. That increases infra complexity but might be necessary.
Maya R: Another cross-cutting concern: auth headers. v1 uses X-API-Key, v2 prefers Authorization: Bearer. We need deterministic mapping in shim and telemetry to identify client versions.
Samir P: Proposal: Gateway for public/hosted traffic with these modes:
1) transform (map headers/payload)
2) passthrough (streaming preserved)
3) redirect (302-style for eligible clients)
We can enable per-route policies.
Leah T: For Dedicated/Private deployments we should avoid central gateway — recommend per-deployment adaptor that runs locally.
Alex Z: Agree — product needs consistent guarantees across hosted/dedicated/private. But implementation can differ. Document should spell differences.
Maya R: Rolling deprecation window: announce 90d -> 60d -> 30d -> sunset. During that time gateway should emit warnings and a header "X-Redwood-Compatibility: v1-deprecated" so SDKs and customers can detect.
Samir P: Telemetry plan: tag requests with compat-version, shim-mode, and transformation delta. Need sampling for payload diffs. Also record latency quantiles per shim mode.
Dave: Ops concerns: autoscaling patterns for gateway under bursty traffic. If gateway becomes hot path, capacity math = (peak qps) * amplification_factor. We need load-test harness.
Alex Z: Action: Samir to draft gateway proxy behavior doc with modes and headers. Leah to document per-service shim contract. Maya to own rollout/deprecation timeline and customer comms. Dave to run perf tests on a prototype.
Samir P: Quick sketch of headers we can use: 
````
X-Redwood-Compat: v1
X-Redwood-Shim-Mode: transform|passthrough|redirect
X-Redwood-Client-Id: <client-id>
X-Redwood-Warning: v1-deprecation-90d
````
Keep them short, avoid PII.
Leah T: For per-service shim, interface example: 
````
POST /_compat/v1proxy HTTP/1.1
Host: model.internal
X-API-Key: <key>
Body: original v1 JSON
````
Service should respond with same v1 shape (status codes + streaming frames) when shim enabled.
Maya R: We should also add a compatibility test matrix to CI that spins up both shim modes and exercises: auth mapping, streaming EOF, error codes, retry semantics. Fail CI on regression.
Samir P: Edgecase: long-poll SSE reconnects. Gateway passthrough must preserve client IP for rate-limiting/backoff heuristics. That means we probably need transparent proxying (X-Forwarded-For) and consistent connection affinity.
Dave: Also consider signature validation for customer-managed keys in Private deployments — if gateway modifies payload you break signatures. So transformation mode must be optional and documented as incompatible with signed payload flows.
Alex Z: Good catch. Add an explicit compatibility matrix in the doc: signed-payload = incompatible with transform mode.
Leah T: Can we provide a library shim for customers to run locally in Private deployments to avoid signature issues? Small drop-in that maps headers without touching body.
Maya R: Yes. That should be part of Private onboarding. Also SDKs should emit the compat header so we can track adoption.
Samir P: Rollout strategy idea: start with read-only endpoints (embeddings) in transform mode to validate mappings, then enable write/generative endpoints behind passthrough fallback.
Alex Z: Decision for now: proceed with Gateway prototype that supports transform+passthrough, but we must keep per-service shim plan as alternative for Private/Dedicated. Document tradeoffs and tests.
Maya R: I'll draft announcement cadence and plan to notify customers 90/60/30 days with examples and migration steps.
Dave: I'll provision k8s job to run 100k qps synthetic tests against prototype and share results.
Samir P: I'll open the design doc PR: /docs/arch/compat/gateway-shim-design.md and include header list, telemetry schema, and CI test matrix.
Leah T: I'll write the per-service shim contract and example middleware for our python microservices.
infra-bot: Note: ticket created in JIRA: RINF-2198 "Gateway compat proxy prototype" assigned to Samir P.
Alex Z: Thanks everyone. We'll sync in next week's arch sync after PR lands. 
Maya R: :thumbsup:
